title: How Westhaven Changed Its Flood Alerts
text:
For years, Westhaven relied mainly on a single river siren to warn residents about fast-rising water. The siren could be heard in the town center, but people in newer neighborhoods often reported that wind, traffic, and closed windows made it difficult to hear. During one overnight storm, several residents also said they heard the siren but did not know whether their own streets were at risk.

The town then tested a layered alert system. Residents can now register for text messages tied to evacuation zones, while the siren remains as a broad outdoor warning. Local radio stations receive the same zone updates, and community volunteers translate urgent messages into three commonly spoken languages. The fire department also posts a simple map showing which zones should prepare, evacuate, or remain alert.

Town officials do not claim that any one channel will reach everyone. Phones can lose power, radio listeners may be asleep, and outdoor sirens are easy to miss indoors. The new plan therefore uses several channels that repeat the same location-specific information in different ways. After the first storm season, officials will compare delivery records and resident surveys to identify neighborhoods that still receive warnings too slowly.
author: Chee Skool
